title: Applied ML evals: integrated onboarding, prompt sets, guardrails, quantization, and regression playbook
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook describes the end-to-end Applied ML evaluation (evals) process at Redwood Inference: model onboarding into the eval-harness, constructing and versioning prompt sets and benchmarks, quality guardrails to prevent regressions, quantization profile validation, and a regression triage playbook. It is intended for ML engineers, applied researchers, and SREs involved in model release and serving.

Scope

- Applies to any new model or major model update intended for serving (hosted, dedicated, or private).
- Covers static prompt/benchmark creation, automated eval harness runs, alerting thresholds, and human-led regression triage.
- Does not replace security/compliance reviews for customer-sensitive models (see security-and-compliance).

Goals

- Ensure model releases maintain or improve production quality along metrics tracked by product teams.
- Catch regressions early via automated eval runs and targeted prompt sets.
- Provide clear escalation steps and owners for triage and rollback decisions.

Ownership and Roles

- Applied ML / Model Onboarding (owner): triage and remediate model-level failures; primary contact for model teams.
- Eval-harness SRE: maintain CI integration, runner health, and metrics capture.
- Platform Observability: ensure dashboards and alert rules are up-to-date.
- Product/Feature owner: provide critical prompt sets and acceptance criteria.

Core Components

1. Eval Harness (redwood-eval-runner)
- Responsible for running deterministic and stochastic evaluations across models and prompt sets.
- Integrations: metrics-db (Influx/Prometheus), artifacts storage (S3), and eval-results-index (Elasticsearch).
- Run types: nightly full-sweep, pre-release gated runs (pull-request), and on-demand targeted runs.

2. Prompt Sets and Benchmarks
- Prompt set structure: name, description, intent tags, seed examples, expected outputs, scoring function.
- Versioning: each prompt set must be versioned (semantic: v1.0.0) and stored in the prompt-sets repo with metadata JSON.
- Benchmarks include: unit-level prompts (edge-cases), regression suites (known failure cases), and product-critical flows (customer-facing sequences).

3. Quality Guardrails
- Metric categories: accuracy (task-specific), safety/toxicity, relevance/faithfulness (for knowledge tasks), latency P95, and cost-per-token delta.
- Thresholds (example):
  - Accept if F1 >= baseline - 0.02 for classification tasks.
  - Reject if safety violation rate increases by > 50% relative to baseline on safety prompt set.
  - Latency P95 must not regress by more than 25% vs baseline for same hardware.
  - Embedding cosine similarity for critical reference prompts must remain >= 0.88.
- Multi-metric decisions: when metrics conflict (e.g., latency improved but accuracy drops), follow the decision matrix (see below).

4. Quantization Profiles
- Each candidate quantization profile (e.g., int8, q4_0, q4_1) must be tested with:
  - Functional evals (same prompt sets as float baseline),
  - Regression-sensitive prompts (to detect hallucination/factuality drift),
  - Performance evals (throughput and latency distributions),
  - Unit-cost analysis (tokens/sec and GPU utilization).
- Profiles with > 1.5% absolute drop in key task metric or safety regressions require mitigation (re-tuning or using higher-precision layers).

Process: Model Onboarding and Eval Integration

1) Pre-onboarding checklist (model owner)

- Confirm model artifact integrity and provenance (checksum, model card).
- Create an onboarding ticket with expected deployment target and primary prompt sets.
- Provide baseline metrics from local evaluation (float baseline): accuracy, latency on representative hardware, and cost estimate.
- Assign temporary reviewers from Applied ML and Product.

2) Add model to eval-harness

- Update eval registry with model ID, container SHA, and supported APIs. Example registry entry (YAML):

  model_id: rwd-candidate-2026-03
  image_sha: sha256:abc123...
  api: text-generation
  supported_profiles: [float32, q4_0]

- Configure pre-release gated runs in CI: run the model against the full regression suite and product-critical prompt sets.
- Ensure artifacts (score outputs, logs) are pushed to eval-results-index.

3) Evaluation run types and cadence

- Pull-request gated: small subset of regression prompts, must pass acceptance thresholds to merge.
- Nightly full-sweep: all prompt sets and quantization profiles; used to surface creeping regressions.
- Canary/Production shadow: optional shadow runs against live traffic samples (produced with PII stripped).

Decision matrix for ambiguous outcomes

- Scenario A (minor metric drop, latency improved): If key product metric drop <= 1% absolute and safety unchanged -> proceed with canary and increased monitoring.
- Scenario B (accuracy drop > 2% or safety regression): block rollout; open regression triage (see below).
- Scenario C (latency P95 regression > 25%): consider alternative quantization profile or model variant; prioritize for performance tuning.

Regression triage playbook (step-by-step)

1. Alerting and initial triage

- When eval-harness raises a regression alert (alert channel: #ml-regressions), the on-call Applied ML engineer acknowledges within 30 minutes.
- Triage checklist: reproduce failure locally, confirm artifact versions, capture failing prompt IDs, and snapshot model container.

2. Classification of regression

- Categories: data-change, model-change, quantization-induced, infra/perf, or test-flake.
- Quick diagnostics:
  - Run model against float baseline prompts -> if float passes but quantized fails, likely quantization.
  - Compare model logits/seeds between versions to detect deterministic shifts.
  - Check infra metrics (GPU memory, OOMs, CPU throttling).

3. Escalation and mitigation

- If safety regression or product-critical failure: page Product and Security leads immediately, create incident ticket, and hold deployment.
- Mitigation options (in order):
  1. Rollback to last good model or quantization profile.
  2. Apply targeted prompt-level filters (temporary guardrail) to block known failing prompts from reaching production routing.
  3. Re-run quantization with higher-precision fallback for sensitive layers.

4. Root cause analysis and follow-up

- Owner: model team must produce an RCA within 3 business days documenting cause, fix, and regression test to prevent recurrence.
- Add new prompt cases to the regression suite if the failure represents a missed edge case.
- If infra-related, update runbook and increase runner capacity or adjust batching heuristics.

Monitoring, Dashboards, and Alerts

- Mandatory dashboards: model-eval-summary, prompt-failure-explorer, quantization-impact. Each must show baseline vs current, 7d trend, and per-prompt failure lists.
- Alerts: threshold-based alerts for guardrail breaches, and anomaly detection for gradual regressions.
- Slack channels: #ml-regressions (alerts), #ml-onboarding (coordination), #ml-qa (postmortems and RCA discussion).

Table: Example gating thresholds

| Metric category | Gate type | Threshold | Action |
|-----------------|-----------|-----------|--------|
| Accuracy (F1) | Hard | >= baseline - 0.02 | Block if lower |
| Safety violations | Hard | <= 1.5x baseline rate | Block and page security |
| Latency P95 | Soft | <= 1.25x baseline | Canary + perf tuning |
| Embedding similarity | Soft | >= 0.88 | Monitor |

Best practices and checklists

- Prompt set hygiene: label prompts with intent, difficulty, and expected behavior; avoid leaking product secrets.
- Repro reproducibility: store random seeds used in stochastic evals and snapshot model RNG state where possible.
- Documentation: every onboarding must include a model card with known limitations and canonical prompt examples.
- Add a minimal smoke test to the service health endpoint that exercises a small, critical prompt.

Examples (command snippets)

- Trigger a gated run locally:
  curl -X POST https://eval-runner.internal/api/runs \ 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $EVAL_TOKEN' \ 
    -d '{"model_id":"rwd-candidate-2026-03","prompt_sets":["product-critical-v1"],"profiles":["float32","q4_0"]}'

- Example prompt-set metadata JSON (stored in prompt-sets repo):
  {
    "name": "product-critical-v1",
    "description": "End-to-end customer flow prompts for payments feature",
    "intents": ["checkout","refund"],
    "version": "v1.0.0"
  }

Appendix: common failure modes and fixes

- Hallucinations increase after quantization: re-run with mixed-precision for attention/key layers; add regression prompts focusing on factuality.
- Inconsistent ranking in reranker models: add contrastive prompt pairs to regression suite and increase evaluation sample size.
- Memory OOMs during nightly runs: reduce batch size or split prompt set across parallel runners.

References and related docs

- eval-harness standards: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/applied-ml-eval-harness-standards-2025
- Quantization best practices: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles/quantization-profiles-best-practices-2026
- Regression triage examples: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/applied-ml-regression-triage-response-and-prioritization-2026

Contact

For questions or to request additions to the regression suite, contact the Applied ML team (applied-ml@redwood.com) or join #ml-onboarding on Slack.
